The code itself is the documentation. And, furthermore, programming
is
difficult. Sure, learning the language itself is easy as the mass of "learn JavaScript in 60 minutes" tutorials out there demonstrate, but learn how to work with an already existing framework is not.
For those who are interested:
Spoiler:
Why Selectable, Command, & ChoiceList?
This is not uncommon for software products, it's actually the reality.
Selectable is a superclass for every window where the player "selects" something from a list, e.g. Items or Skills.
Technically, it makes a difference whether you select an Item from a list, or a command such as "New Game" from the title screen, this is why we also have Window_Command. But because Window_Command inherits from Window_Selectable anyway it could sometimes a bit tricky to decide which window class to pick.
ChoiceList is only used for the Message Choices and, from my experience, is too situationally to be reused in other plugins.
What also helps is to look at already existing windows that look similar to yours like Window_TitleCommand

I wasn't aware that you are using MV. The constructors for windows are a bit inconsistent in MV, luckily they improved that a lot in MZ. Anyway, let's go!
Khali said:
This is fine, I can change initialize, but it was easier for me to just use .windowWidth() and .windowHeight(), why wouldn't I? They're alread there.
Click to expand...
Exactly, you want to use windowWidth (and maybe windowHeight), like this:
Code:
Custom_Window.prototype.windowWidth = function() {
  return 200;
}
Then you don't need a custom constructor for your window class, and I also recommend not having one, because the constructor of Window_Command is already robust.
You can also use that code snippet for the height, but by default, the Window_Command class does that automatically for you to fit it to the number of commands in the list (which is a bonus over the Window_Selectable).
Khali said:
The one I still don't understand is, it doesn't have it's own x or y, but kept setting x and y to 0 and despite everything I tried it just wouldn't stop doing this. Window_TitleCommand has an updatePlacement function, but I don't see anything like that in Window_Command, although I guess I could just make one.
Click to expand...
I agree, this looks a bit awkward and is probably a reason why they changed it in MZ. It's perhaps the easiest to reposition the window not in the window class itself, but in the scene where you create it and add it to the screen.
Code:
...
const gameWindow = new Custom_Window(0, 0);
gameWindow.x = Graphics.boxWidth / 2 - gameWindow.width / 2;
gameWindow.y = Graphics.boxHeight / 2 - gameWindow.height / 2;
...
I could continue and dive deeper but when your plugin is already working using the Window_Selectable class then it's just fine
Personally, I think using Window_Command is best practice, but using Window_Selectable is not a bad practice either.
